title: Cross-process Accept-versus-expiry races for 1v1 and TagDuel
priority: P1 — prove that acceptance immediately before the deadline racing the timeout sweeper yields exactly one consistent state, with no partial acceptance or orphaned physical-seat locks.

design.isolation: temporary SQLite database seeded by the parent; parent connection closed before child processes start
design.concurrency: six races across separate Node processes: three 1v1 Accept-vs-expiry races and three TagDuel final-seat Accept-vs-expiry races; each race uses separate better-sqlite3 connections and a synchronized start barrier
design.clock: Accept workers use deadline-1ms; sweeper workers use the exact deadline; an idempotent sweeper retry reconciles transient SQLITE_BUSY outcomes

assertions: each 1v1 invitation settles to playing or expired; never remains pending after the deterministic retry
a playing 1v1 has both physical duel_members locks and no tag_members locks; an expired invitation has no locks
each TagDuel lobby settles to playing or expired; never remains a partially accepted lobby after retry
a playing TagDuel has all four accepted seats and exactly four tag_members locks; an expired lobby has no tag_members or duel_members locks
all physical card UIDs remain unique in successfully started games
players, player_cards, starter_grants, decks and deck_cards remain byte-equivalent before and after all races
limitations: SQLite temporário e processos Node independentes; sem banco persistente.
O teste verifica stores/transações reais, não gateway/guild Discord real.
A corrida usa relógios determinísticos nos processos; o retry explícito cobre falha transitória de lock, não mede latência de produção.
Não integra nem certifica cartas; não altera comandos ou runtime.

testExecution.extendedSoak: not configured as a separate M543 workflow
